471442.name: Triticale 813 Hexaploide by StarSeed Seed
471442.short_description: StarSeed’s high-biomass winter annual cover crop. A wheat-rye hybrid engineered for maximum biomass, winter hardiness, and superior forage quality — reported to be less allelopathic than cereal rye.
471442.description:
Triticale 813 Hexaploide is StarSeed's flagship winter annual cover crop and forage grain — a carefully selected hexaploid triticale variety bred for high biomass production, excellent winter hardiness, and superior forage quality. Triticale is a hybrid grain crop produced by crossing wheat (Triticum) and rye (Secale), combining wheat's yield potential and palatability with rye's cold tolerance and vigor. StarSeed's 813 variety takes these base advantages further with selection specifically for high dry matter production, disease resistance, and reduced allelopathic activity compared to standard cereal rye.

Allelopathy — the chemical suppression of other plant species — is one agronomic consideration with cereal rye as a cover crop (much of rye's effect on a following crop is also due to nitrogen tie-up). Cereal rye releases allelopathic compounds from its residue that can delay or suppress establishment of the following cash crop, particularly small-seeded vegetable crops and some legumes. Triticale 813 is reported to have lower allelopathic activity than cereal rye, which can make it a more crop-rotation-friendly winter annual cover crop in mixed and vegetable farming systems where the following crop's establishment timing is critical.

For livestock producers, Triticale 813 offers a clear protein advantage over cereal rye. Triticale grain and forage consistently tests 2–4 percentage points higher in crude protein than comparable cereal rye, making it a more nutritionally valuable winter annual forage for cattle, sheep, and other ruminants. Its soft grain and excellent palatability also make it more readily consumed than rye, reducing selective grazing.

As a cover crop anchor species, Triticale 813 pairs exceptionally well with hairy vetch or crimson clover in winter cover crop mixes. The triticale provides the structural biomass and weed-suppression canopy while the legume companion fixes nitrogen — together delivering both the carbon and nitrogen components of a high-performance winter cover crop system. Seeding rates drop significantly when using Triticale 813 in a mix versus as a pure stand.

471441.name: Greenfield Blend by StarSeed Seed
471441.short_description: A multi-species cover crop and pasture improvement blend designed for homesteaders and small-farm operators. Grasses, legumes, and broadleaf herbs for 1–40 acre operations.
471441.description:
The Greenfield Blend is StarSeed's purpose-built multi-species mix for homesteaders and small-farm operators who want the soil-building and forage benefits of diverse species without the complexity of formulating a custom blend. Developed by StarSeed — a NativeSeed Group company, and a sister brand to Nature's Seed — this blend is engineered to deliver multiple ecosystem functions simultaneously: nitrogen fixation from legumes, high biomass and weed suppression from grasses, early-season pollinator forage from flowering broadleaf species, and rapid erosion control on disturbed soils.

The Greenfield Blend is positioned as the gateway product for growers transitioning from single-species monocultures toward multi-species systems. It is intentionally designed for 1–40 acre operations — a scale that excludes most large commercial row crop operations but covers the broad range of homestead farms, hobby farms, market gardens, and small ranching operations where the grower is looking for a practical, proven blend rather than a fully customized species list.

The blend combines annual and short-lived perennial species to deliver two complementary functions: rapid establishment in year one (from annual components) and persistence and deepening soil function in year two and beyond (from perennial components). This architecture means the Greenfield Blend continues delivering value across multiple seasons without immediate replanting — unlike a single-species annual cover crop that must be reseeded every year.

For growers new to multi-species cover cropping, the Greenfield Blend removes the primary barrier to entry: the need to source and blend multiple separate species. It ships as a single, ready-to-sow bag. The exact species composition varies seasonally and by availability from StarSeed's production network — growers who need a fixed species list for research or certification purposes should request a current composition sheet or consider a custom blend.

This blend is best used as a cover crop between cash crop seasons, a pasture improvement overseeding tool, or a transitional mix for land coming out of conventional row crop production.

471439.name: Indian Ricegrass Seed
471439.short_description: One of the most drought-tolerant native grasses of the arid West. Fine-textured bunchgrass for xeriscape, erosion control, and arid-land restoration. Survives on 6–8 inches annual rainfall once established.
471439.description:
Indian Ricegrass (Achnatherum hymenoides, formerly Oryzopsis hymenoides) is one of the most drought-tolerant grasses native to North America. Found naturally across the Great Basin, Intermountain West, and desert Southwest — from the sandy plains of the Mojave to the rocky foothills of the Rockies — this cool-season bunchgrass has evolved over thousands of years in conditions that would kill most turfgrasses within weeks. Established plants survive on as little as 6–8 inches of annual rainfall, making it one of the most water-efficient native grasses for xeriscape landscapes in arid regions.

The name comes from its historical importance to Indigenous peoples of the Great Basin and Southwest. Many Native American tribes — including the Navajo, Shoshone, Paiute, and Hopi — harvested the seeds as a food staple for thousands of years. The small, black, nutritious seeds were ground into flour and used in breads and porridges. This cultural history earned the plant its common name and reflects its role as a foundational species in Great Basin ecosystems long before European contact.

In modern landscapes, Indian Ricegrass is valued for its fine-textured, arching foliage and ornamental seed heads. Plants grow 18–30 inches tall in airy clumps, producing distinctive open seed heads with tiny black seeds in spring. The foliage is fine-bladed and green through the cool season, turning straw-gold in summer — providing year-round textural interest even during summer dormancy. It is a standard species in Southwest xeriscape designs and native grass restoration projects across the western states.

Fall sowing is essential for reliable stand establishment. Indian Ricegrass seed has a hard seed coat and embryo dormancy that make germination slow and uneven — fall-planted or properly conditioned (scarified) seed combined with winter chilling improves results, but germination is rarely uniform. Spring-seeded stands are consistently disappointing in both germination percentage and establishment rate. Allow two full growing seasons before expecting full coverage.

471438.name: Firecracker Penstemon Seed
471438.short_description: Among the earliest-blooming scarlet penstemons in the desert Southwest. Tubular red flowers in late winter through spring draw hummingbirds before most other wildflowers emerge. A water-wise native for Southwest xeriscapes.
471438.description:
Firecracker Penstemon is the first sign of spring in many desert and Great Basin landscapes — its scarlet, tubular flowers emerging as early as January in low-desert Arizona and Nevada, well before most other native wildflowers break dormancy. Native across the Intermountain West and Colorado Plateau — Utah, Nevada, Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico, and parts of California, Idaho, and Wyoming — Penstemon eatonii is a true cold-hardy desert perennial, surviving from zone 4 cold to the intense heat of zone 10 low desert.

The plant's primary ecological function is as a hummingbird fuel station. Broad-billed, Costa's, and Anna's hummingbirds depend on early-blooming penstemons as critical refueling stops during late-winter territory establishment and early migration. Firecracker Penstemon is ideally timed: its bloom window (January–April depending on elevation) coincides precisely with the period when hummingbird energy demands are highest and competing nectar sources are scarcest.

Firecracker Penstemon forms an attractive rosette of evergreen, leathery basal leaves 18–36 inches wide. From this base, tall, upright flower stalks rise 18–36 inches, densely packed with scarlet tubular flowers. The plant is functionally evergreen in mild winters — the basal foliage persists through cold, greening up and expanding in late winter just ahead of bloom.

It is widely recommended for low-water and xeriscape landscapes across the Intermountain West. Some regional water utilities offer turf-conversion rebates for qualifying projects; plant lists and eligibility vary by program and change over time, so verify current requirements with your local water utility.

Sowing requires patience and planning. Cold stratification is non-negotiable for reliable germination. Fall sowing (October–November) is the preferred approach — seed stratifies naturally over winter and germinates the following spring. Spring-sown seed must be cold-stratified for 30–60 days in a sealed bag in the refrigerator before planting. First-season plants produce only a rosette of basal leaves. Blooms appear in year two.

471437.name: Big Bluestem Grass Seed
categories: Northern US Pasture Seeds & Seed Mixes
Transitional Zone Pasture Seeds & Seed Mixes
471437.short_description: The monarch of the tallgrass prairie. Big Bluestem once blanketed 250 million acres of North America and remains the gold standard for native pasture, carbon sequestration, and prairie restoration.
471437.description:
Big Bluestem is the dominant grass of the original North American tallgrass prairie — the species that defined the Great Plains before the plow. Standing 4 to 8 feet tall with roots that penetrate 6 to 10 feet into the soil, it is one of the deepest-rooted grasses on the continent. That root architecture is the foundation of its reputation as a carbon sequestration species and its exceptional drought tolerance once established.

For forage producers, Big Bluestem delivers 65 to 70 percent digestibility when cattle graze it before the boot stage. Palatability drops quickly as the plant matures, so timing grazing is critical — this is a grass that rewards management. Native hay operations have relied on it for generations because it produces dense, nutritious forage on soils that struggle to support introduced species.

As a habitat plant, Big Bluestem is irreplaceable. Its tall, dense bunches provide nesting and escape cover for bobwhite quail, pheasant, and ground-nesting songbirds. It qualifies for CRP and EQIP cost-share practices in most states, making it a practical economic choice for conservation farmers and ranchers.

Fall transforms Big Bluestem into one of the most visually striking native plants on the landscape. Stems turn burgundy and copper as temperatures drop, holding color well into winter. This ornamental value has made it a common choice for large-scale native landscape plantings and prairie restorations where aesthetics matter alongside function.

Patience is required. Big Bluestem takes 2 to 3 seasons to reach full production, investing most of its first-year energy into root development. Year one will look underwhelming. That is normal — it is not failure. Do not mow below 4 inches during the first two growing seasons, and do not expect hay production until year 3. The long-term payoff is a stand that will persist for decades with minimal inputs.

471436.name: Sweetclover Seed — Yellow & White
471436.short_description: One of the most powerful nitrogen-fixing biennials available, fixing 100–200 lbs N/acre over two seasons. A deep taproot (up to ~5 ft) conditions subsoil compaction, and the year-two bloom is one of the most valued honey plants in the Northern Plains and Midwest.
471436.description:
Sweetclover is old-fashioned cover cropping at its most effective. Before synthetic nitrogen, sweetclover was the nitrogen source for millions of acres of dryland grain production across the Great Plains. It came back into favor among regenerative farmers for the same reason it was valued in the first place: it fixes more nitrogen per acre than almost any other practical cover crop option, its taproot reaches depths that most legumes don’t approach, and it does both jobs with very low input requirements.

Yellow sweetclover (Melilotus officinalis) and white sweetclover (Melilotus alba) are closely related biennial legumes with very similar agronomic profiles. Yellow tends to be slightly earlier-maturing and is often considered marginally more winter-hardy at the extremes. White typically produces somewhat larger biomass and a heavier bloom. Growing them together hedges against the differences between the two and provides a slightly extended bloom period—useful for both bee forage and pollinator habitat goals.

The nitrogen fixation numbers are genuine. In university research across multiple states, sweetclover has consistently fixed 100–200 lbs of nitrogen per acre over a two-season cycle. That nitrogen becomes available to the following cash crop as the residue mineralizes—a real input cost reduction for grain farmers. The taproot, reaching 5–8 feet, does subsoil work that most other legume covers cannot match.

The year-two bloom is exceptional bee forage. In many states, beekeepers and extension services rate sweetclover as the single most valuable honey plant available. The bloom is dense, long-lasting, and highly attractive to managed honeybees and native pollinators alike.

There are serious limitations with sweetclover that you must understand before using it as hay or silage. Sweetclover contains coumarin. When sweetclover hay or silage is improperly cured and molds, coumarin converts to dicoumarol, an anticoagulant that causes fatal internal bleeding in cattle. This is a documented, serious livestock health risk. Do not feed moldy sweetclover hay to cattle. This applies specifically to poorly cured hay and silage—fresh forage and well-cured hay are safe.

471435.name: Forage Chicory Seed
471435.short_description: A deep-rooted perennial forb that mines calcium, phosphorus, and magnesium from deep in the subsoil. At about 15–25% crude protein, it is one of the highest-quality summer forages available for sheep, goats, and deer.
471435.description:
Forage chicory does something that almost no other pasture plant can do at scale: it sends a deep taproot — commonly several feet, up to about 6 feet in deep soils — into the subsoil to pull up mineral nutrients—calcium, phosphorus, magnesium—that are locked beyond the reach of grasses and most legumes. Those minerals cycle back to the surface through the plant, become available to livestock that graze it, and ultimately feed the topsoil system when the plant dies back. This is genuine mineral cycling, not marketing language.

The forage quality numbers are exceptional. Chicory runs about 15–25% crude protein, comparable to alfalfa and above perennial ryegrass or orchardgrass at similar growth stages, with high digestibility. It is particularly valued for sheep and goats because of an additional documented benefit: anthelmintic properties. Research from New Zealand and the UK, where chicory-based pastures have been studied extensively, shows that grazing chicory reduces intestinal parasite loads in small ruminants. This is a meaningful practical benefit for producers managing parasite pressure without heavy chemical treatment.

Chicory is also a proven deer attractant and food plot plant. Deer graze it heavily in summer and early fall when other warm-season food sources are limited. Its combination of high protein, palatability, and broad seasonal availability makes it one of the most used food plot perennials in the eastern and midwestern U.S.

We will not oversell chicory’s ease of establishment. It takes 45–60 days to reach grazeable height and is competitive with pasture grasses during that window. Set-stocking—continuous grazing pressure—degrades chicory stands faster than any other management mistake. Properly managed with rotational grazing and rest periods, stands persist 3–5 years. Mismanaged, they fade in 1–2. Plan your grazing system before you plant.

471434.name: Forage Turnip Seed
471434.short_description: A dual-purpose cool-season annual that produces a compaction-busting taproot and high-quality forage in 45–75 days. Deer, cattle, sheep, and pigs all actively seek it out—and it improves your soil at the same time.
471434.description:
Forage turnip earns a rare designation in cover cropping: it does two important jobs simultaneously and does both well. Below ground, the taproot drives 12–18 inches into compacted soil, physically fracturing hardpan layers that restrict water movement and root development. Above ground, both the leafy tops and the bulb provide high-quality, highly digestible forage that livestock and deer will actively seek out over competing forages.

The speed of this crop is remarkable. Forage turnip goes from seed to a full-size plant in about 60–90 days under cool conditions (tops grazeable in ~60–70 days)—one of the faster-establishing brassica cover crops. That makes it extremely practical for late-summer and early-fall planting after small grain harvest, or as a quick cover before winter in Zone 3–9 climates.

Food plot hunters value forage turnip because deer will hammer it aggressively starting in late fall, after the first frost sweetens the bulb. Early-season food plots often get passed over; late-season turnip plots get worked until the ground freezes. Sheep, cattle, and pigs graze the tops readily and will root out the bulbs as well.

There are real limitations with forage turnip that you need to plan around. It is a cool-season crop—do not plant in summer in Zone 6 and above, or in heat waves in Zone 5. It will bolt and decline rapidly in warm temperatures. Forage turnip is in the brassica family, which means you need to rotate away from other brassicas (including canola, mustard, and other cover crop brassicas) to prevent clubroot disease and other soilborne pathogen buildup. Brassicas should make up no more than about one-third of any grazing animal's diet, be introduced gradually, and be fed alongside hay or grass — fed as the sole forage they can cause nitrate poisoning, polioencephalomalacia, hemolytic anemia, and bloat. And the sulfur-containing glucosinolate compounds that give brassicas their health-promoting properties also produce a strong odor when the crop is incorporated—not a problem agronomically, but worth knowing.

471433.name: Cowpeas Seed
471433.short_description: Cowpeas establish fast in summer heat, fix 60-150 lbs of nitrogen per acre, and tolerate drought better than most warm-season legumes. They also attract quail, deer, and turkey — making them one of the best dual-purpose cover crop and food plot species available.
471433.description:
Cowpeas (Vigna unguiculata) are a warm-season annual legume with origins in sub-Saharan Africa, where they have been cultivated for over 5,000 years as a food and forage crop in hot, dry conditions. In North American agriculture, cowpeas occupy a distinct niche: they are one of the most drought-tolerant annual legumes available for summer use, establishing reliably in conditions that would stress or kill other warm-season cover crops including sunn hemp and berseem clover. Their deep, fibrous root system actively mines subsoil moisture and breaks up compaction layers while the surface vegetation suppresses weeds and fixes nitrogen.

Cowpeas fix roughly 60-150 lbs of nitrogen per acre — a range that reflects significant variability in performance based on variety, stand density, rainfall, and termination timing. The high end of that range requires good inoculation, a full-season stand, and incorporation at pod-fill rather than early in the season. The low end reflects short-window plantings or marginal growing conditions. In either case, the nitrogen credit is real and supplements synthetic fertilizer needs in the following crop.

Beyond their agronomic role, cowpeas are one of the premier food plot species for wildlife management across the Southeast and Gulf Coast. White-tailed deer, bobwhite quail, wild turkey, and doves all use cowpea fields heavily from early summer through fall. This dual-use profile — agronomic cover crop plus wildlife food plot — makes cowpeas particularly valuable for landowners who manage both crop production and wildlife habitat. Cowpeas can be planted, allowed to produce seed pods, and left standing for wildlife to forage through, which is a different management approach than a pure cover crop termination system.

Cowpeas require warm soil (minimum 65°F) to germinate reliably. They are killed by frost, do not establish in cool weather, and should not be planted until at least 2 weeks after the corn planting date in any given region. In zones 7-11 they are a natural summer fit. In zones 5-6, the growing window exists but is compressed.

471432.name: Balansa Clover Seed
471432.short_description: Balansa clover tolerates waterlogged soils that kill other clovers. It fixes roughly 50-100 lbs of nitrogen per acre and provides exceptional pollinator forage through a long bloom period. The right clover for low-lying and wet-weather ground.
471432.description:
Balansa clover (Trifolium michelianum) is an annual legume that fills a specific ecological niche that most clovers cannot occupy: wet, waterlogged, or poorly-drained soils. While red clover, crimson clover, and berseem clover all suffer root rot and stand loss in saturated soils, balansa clover maintains growth and nodule function even in temporary flooding — a trait that makes it uniquely valuable for low-lying agricultural ground, irrigated systems, and regions with frequent wet-season rainfall.

Beyond its waterlogging tolerance, balansa clover is a productive nitrogen fixer, capable of fixing roughly 50-100 lbs of nitrogen per acre in a full growing season. It is a small-seeded clover that requires a fine, firm seedbed and shallow planting (1/8-1/4 inch depth), but once established it produces prolific growth and a long bloom period that provides exceptional forage for honeybees and native pollinators.

Balansa clover is best adapted to zones 6-10, with particularly strong performance along the Pacific Coast, in the Southeast, and in subtropical climates with mild winters. It does not have meaningful cold hardiness in northern zones and should not be treated as a winter cover crop in climates that see sustained temperatures below 20°F.

Its limitation set is real: balansa clover underperforms on dry, sandy soils where drainage is too rapid, it will not overwinter in cold northern climates, and like all annual clovers it must be replanted each year. It is also less commonly available than red or crimson clover, which means fewer local extension data points — most performance data comes from Australia, New Zealand, and Pacific Coast U.S. trials. We work from those data sets and our own observations. Growers in the Southeast and Pacific Coast will find balansa well-suited to local conditions.

471431.name: Berseem Clover Seed
471431.short_description: Berseem clover is a fast-establishing annual legume that fixes 100-200 lbs of nitrogen per acre and is widely regarded as low-bloat — no cases of bloat from grazing berseem have been reported. It doubles as high-quality forage and excellent bee pasture.
471431.description:
Berseem clover (Trifolium alexandrinum), also called Egyptian clover, is a warm-season annual legume native to the Mediterranean region that has been cultivated for thousands of years as a high-quality forage and soil-improvement crop. In North American cover crop systems, it occupies a distinct niche: it establishes faster than almost any other clover, tolerates summer planting in warm climates, and uniquely among clovers, poses no bloat risk to cattle — a property that makes it practical for integrated cover-crop-forage systems where cattle move through cover crop fields.

From a nitrogen fixation standpoint, berseem clover is highly productive. Under good growing conditions with proper inoculation, it can fix 100-200 lbs of nitrogen per acre over a single growing season, comparable to hairy vetch. Unlike vetch, it grows upright to 12-24 inches rather than vining, which simplifies equipment management at termination.

Berseem clover germinates in just 5-7 days under warm soil conditions and produces usable forage biomass within 30-45 days of planting. In warm-climate double-cut forage systems, it is cut at first bloom, allowed to regrow, and cut again 4-6 weeks later for a second yield — this is rare among annual clovers and increases total season biomass significantly. It also produces abundant, accessible flowers that are highly attractive to honeybees and native bees.

Berseem clover is not adapted to cold climates. It does not overwinter reliably below zone 6, and it performs poorly in soils with pH below 6.0 or in heavy clay or waterlogged conditions. It is a warm-season annual and should be managed as such — expect to replant annually. Its performance in northern states is limited to summer plantings where it functions as a short-season nitrogen fixer between cash crops.

471430.name: Hairy Vetch Seed
471430.short_description: Hairy vetch is a high-biomass winter annual legume that fixes 80-200 lbs of nitrogen per acre. It is one of the most effective weed-suppressing cover crops available for corn and vegetable rotations.
471430.description:
Hairy vetch (Vicia villosa) is a winter annual legume used primarily as a cover crop in grain and vegetable production systems. It is one of the highest-biomass, highest-nitrogen-fixing cover crops available in temperate North America, capable of producing 3-6 tons of dry matter per acre and fixing 80-200 lbs of nitrogen per acre when incorporated at full bloom. That nitrogen is also highly available to the following cash crop — studies consistently show corn following hairy vetch can reduce synthetic N applications by 60-100 lbs per acre.

Hairy vetch is a vining plant that sprawls across the soil surface and through companion crops, forming a dense mat that suppresses weeds effectively. It is most commonly grown with winter rye as a companion; the rye provides physical support for the vetch and makes the combined mulch easier to manage at termination. The partnership also improves winter hardiness and stand reliability in marginal zones.

Ideal use cases include pre-corn cover crops in grain systems, rolled or crimped no-till mulch beds for vegetable transplanting, and weed suppression in organic systems. Hairy vetch is best planted in late summer or early fall in zones 4-9, and it overwinters reliably in zones 5-9; it is winter-hardy through zone 4 and into zone 3 with dependable snow cover. On exposed sites in zones 3-4 without snow cover, winterkill risk rises, though it often reseeds and re-establishes as temperatures moderate.

Hairy vetch has real limitations and we will not oversell it. The vining growth habit can tangle in tillage and planting equipment if termination timing is missed. Do not plant hairy vetch alone on steep slopes where biomass will be difficult to manage. It must be inoculated with Rhizobium leguminosarum if not previously grown in the field. Most critically: hairy vetch can cause photosensitization and, in some cases, a systemic (granulomatous) disease in horses and cattle that can be serious or fatal — do not allow grazing on vetch stands or vetch-residue fields, and keep animals away from the seed, which also carries anti-nutritional compounds.

470555.name: Plains Prairie Native Seed Mix
470555.short_description: Twelve-species native seed mix rebuilding the mixed-grass prairie of the Great Plains — big bluestem, indiangrass, western wheatgrass, sideoats grama, switchgrass, Canada and Virginia wildrye, plus four native forbs. All native, warm and cool season, drought tolerant once established.

470547.name: Southern Livestock Pasture Seed Mix
categories: Southern US Pasture Seeds & Seed Mixes
470547.short_description: Nine species — tall fescue, perennial ryegrass, Sahara II bermudagrass, alfalfa, Ladino white clover, cicer milkvetch, Puna chicory, orchardgrass, and birdsfoot trefoil — covering cool-season, warm-season, and legume fractions for year-round southern pasture production.

470543.name: California Native Ignition Resistant Seed Mix
categories: Drought-Tolerant Lawn Seeds — Built for CA, AZ, OR & the Southwest
470543.short_description: Seven California native species — purple needlegrass, blue wildrye, Sandberg bluegrass, small fescue, deerweed, miniature lupine, and Great Valley gumweed — in a bunchgrass-and-forb structure that reduces fuel load and holds slopes without irrigation. Designed for CAL FIRE Zone 2 defensible space.

464558.name: Eastern Gamagrass (Fakahatchee) Seed
464558.short_description: Fakahatchee Grass (Tripsacum dactyloides) is a striking native perennial grass that forms dense, arching clumps up to 5–6 ft tall. Hardy in Zones 5–11, it thrives in sun to part shade and wet to dry soils — ideal for Florida-friendly landscapes, rain gardens, and native habitat restoration.
464558.description:
Fakahatchee Grass is one of the most iconic native grasses of Florida and the southeastern United States. Also known as Eastern Gamagrass, this warm-season perennial forms dense, arching clumps of bright green foliage that bring year-round structure and movement to your landscape. In subtropical climates, it stays evergreen — making it one of the few native grasses that looks great in every season.

Unlike non-native ornamental grasses, Fakahatchee Grass supports local ecosystems. Its seeds feed songbirds, quail, and wild turkeys. The dense clumps provide shelter for small mammals, reptiles, and ground-nesting birds. It serves as a larval host for the Byssus Skipper butterfly, and its inconspicuous flower spikes attract native pollinators throughout late spring and summer.

Native to Florida, the Gulf Coast, and much of the eastern U.S. from Texas to Connecticut. Thrives in full sun to partial shade and tolerates a wide range of soil moisture — from well-drained uplands to seasonally flooded sites. Once established, it is moderately drought tolerant and requires almost no maintenance. Hardy in USDA Zones 5–11, with best performance in Zones 8–11. Direct sow in spring after last frost, or cold-stratify seed at 35–40°F for 6–10 weeks before planting for best germination.

462219.name: Texas Bluebonnet Seeds
462219.short_description: Texas Bluebonnet (Lupinus texensis) — the official Texas state flower. Pre-scarified seed for reliable germination. Fall-planted winter annual that reseeds year after year.
462219.description:
Texas Bluebonnet (Lupinus texensis) is the official state flower of Texas and one of the most iconic wildflowers in North America. Each spring, Bluebonnets transform roadsides, meadows, and home gardens into seas of brilliant blue-purple color — a defining image of the Texas Hill Country and one that every Texan recognizes from childhood.

Beyond their beauty, Bluebonnets are a native legume that enriches the soil with nitrogen and provides early-season nectar for native bees and other pollinators. They reseed naturally when allowed to set seed, building a self-sustaining colony over time. Once established in the right conditions, a Bluebonnet planting comes back reliably each year with minimal care.

For best results in Texas and surrounding states, sow in fall (September–November) into a prepared, well-draining seedbed. Scarify seed before planting or purchase pre-scarified. Our 1 lb bag covers up to 200–300 sq ft in garden applications. Seed you can trust — from a team that knows Texas wildflowers.

462220.name: Texas Native Wildflower Mix
462220.short_description: 8-species native wildflower blend anchored by Texas Bluebonnet at 22%. Covers March through October with native annuals and perennials adapted to Texas soils.

462222.name: Texas Native Grass Seed Mix
categories: Drought-Tolerant Lawn Seeds — Built for CA, AZ, OR & the Southwest
462222.short_description: 3-species native grass blend dominated by Buffalograss at 70%. Uses 30-40% less water than Bermuda. Built for Central and West Texas alkaline soils.

462221.name: Texas Pollinator Wildflower Mix
462221.short_description: 8-species native pollinator blend with Milkweed for Monarchs, Liatris for native bees, and Scarlet Sage for hummingbirds. Blooms March through October.

462260.name: Pink Evening Primrose Seeds
462260.short_description: Pink Evening Primrose (Oenothera speciosa) — the iconic Texas pink roadside wildflower. Native perennial that creates carpets of pink blooms April through October. Drought-proof once established.

462223.name: Texas Native Pasture Prairie Mix
categories: Drought-Tolerant Lawn Seeds — Built for CA, AZ, OR & the Southwest
462223.short_description:
The Texas state grass — sideoats grama — anchors this all-native xeriscape blend built for Hill Country yards, pasture borders, and low-maintenance lawns across the Southwest.

8-species native grass and wildflower blend anchored by Sideoats Grama at 35% and Little Bluestem at 25%. Built for rangeland restoration, conservation programs, and livestock pasture.

Livestock Suitability: Excellent for cattle and horses — 85% native warm-season grasses provide high-quality summer forage with heavy grazing tolerance. Good for goats. Use caution with sheep — Texas Bluebonnet (5% of mix) is a lupine species; avoid grazing sheep on young stands where wildflowers dominate. Bloat risk: Very low — only 5% legume content; bloat requires 50%+ legume pastures.

462264.name: Drummond Phlox Seeds
462264.short_description: Drummond Phlox (Phlox drummondii) — the only annual phlox native to Texas. Multicolor blooms in red, pink, purple, and white from March through May. Perfect bluebonnet companion.

462294.short_description: Lanceleaf Coreopsis (Coreopsis lanceolata) — Florida’s state wildflower genus. Drought-tolerant perennial with bright yellow blooms. Thrives in sandy soil. Zones 3-8.

462289.name: Florida Coastal Native Wildflower Seed Mix
462289.short_description: Focused 3-species coastal wildflower blend — Blanket Flower, Lanceleaf Coreopsis, and Spotted Beebalm. Built for Florida’s toughest sandy, coastal conditions. Zero filler.

462284.name: Grass Seed Mix for Florida Lawns
462284.short_description: Bahiagrass 50% and Bermudagrass 30% — seed your Florida lawn for a fraction of sod cost. Less water, less fertilizer, fewer bugs than St. Augustine.

462280.name: Florida Pollinator and Butterfly Seed Mix
462280.short_description: 6-species native pollinator blend with Swamp Milkweed for Monarchs, Blazing Star for native bees, and Scarlet Sage for hummingbirds. Year-round butterfly habitat for Florida.

462276.name: Florida Native Wildflower Seed Mix
462276.short_description: 7-species native wildflower blend anchored by Lanceleaf Coreopsis at 22% — Florida’s state wildflower. Covers May through October. Designed for Florida’s sandy soils.

461690.name: Pollinator Corridor Kit
461690.short_description: Create a permanent pollinator habitat with our 3-species corridor kit: Central Valley Pollinator Wildflower Mix for nectar, California Native Grass for structure, and White Clover for season-long bloom. 6.5 lbs covers ~500-2,000 sq ft.
461690.description: A 3-component habitat kit designed to create permanent pollinator corridors along field edges, fence lines, garden borders, and unused strips. Combines nectar-rich wildflowers for foraging, native bunchgrasses for nesting habitat, and White Clover for reliable season-long bloom. Ships as three separate bags.

461689.name: First-Year Color + Perennial Foundation Wildflower Kit
461689.short_description: Get wildflower color in year one and lasting perennial blooms for years to come. Annual Wildflower Mix for instant color plus Deer Resistant Mix for long-term foundation. 1 lb covers ~1,000 sq ft.
461689.description: A 2-mix wildflower kit designed to solve the biggest problem with perennial wildflower plantings: the wait. The Annual Mix provides dense color in the first growing season while the Deer Resistant Mix establishes a long-term perennial foundation underneath. Year 1 you get flowers from the annuals. Year 2 onward, the perennials take over and bloom for decades.

461687.name: Weed Smother Cover Crop Kit
461687.short_description: Smother weeds naturally with our 2-species cover crop kit: heavy Cereal Rye for allelopathic weed suppression and Mustard Biofumigant for soilborne weed seed destruction. 15 lbs covers ~5,000 sq ft.
461687.description: A 2-species weed suppression kit built around the two most aggressive weed-fighting cover crops available: Winter Cereal Rye and Mustard Biofumigant. The rye suppresses weeds from above (allelopathic chemicals + dense canopy shading) while mustard destroys weed seeds in the soil from below (glucosinolate biofumigation).

461686.name: Soil Builder Cover Crop Kit
461686.short_description: Build soil health with our 3-species cover crop kit: Winter Cereal Rye for organic matter, White Clover for nitrogen, and Mustard Biofumigant for disease suppression. 20 lbs covers ~5,000 sq ft.
461686.description: A 3-species cover crop kit that attacks soil health from three angles: Winter Cereal Rye builds organic matter and suppresses weeds, White Clover fixes nitrogen, and Mustard Biofumigant kills soilborne pathogens and nematodes. Ships as three separate bags for fall or spring planting.

461685.name: Overseed & Repair Lawn Kit
categories: Drought-Tolerant Lawn Seeds — Built for CA, AZ, OR & the Southwest
461685.short_description: Repair bare spots and thicken thin lawns with our 2-seed kit: Triblade Elite Tall Fescue for long-term density and Perennial Ryegrass for fast green-up. 10 lbs covers ~2,000 sq ft.
461685.description: A 2-species lawn repair kit that pairs fast-germinating Perennial Ryegrass with deep-rooted Triblade Elite Tall Fescue. The ryegrass gives you visible green in 5-10 days while the fescue fills in behind it for a dense, drought-tolerant, permanent lawn. Ships as two separate 5 lb bags.

461684.name: Thin Pasture Fix Kit
461684.short_description: Rebuild thin pastures with our 3-species kit: Perennial Ryegrass, White Clover, and Orchardgrass. 15 lbs covers approximately 10,000 sq ft. Ships as 3 separate bags for flexible application.
461684.description: A 3-species pasture renovation kit designed to fill in bare spots, thicken thin stands, and improve forage quality in degraded pastures. Ships as three separate bags — Perennial Ryegrass (5 lb), White Clover (5 lb), and Orchardgrass (5 lb) — so you can broadcast all three together or adjust ratios for your specific conditions.

458473.name: Upland Game Mix
458473.short_description: Upland Game Mix is a versatile seed blend designed for wildlife food plots and cover strips that support upland game birds like pheasants and quail from mid-summer through fall and into early winter. The blend pairs white proso millet and browntop millet (33.5% each) with buckwheat (33%), delivering a staggered, multi-seed buffet and fast-growing foliage. This combination provides continuous seed production, palatable seeds, and layered canopy structure; tall millet stems over a buckwheat understory, offering overhead concealment and lateral cover for roosting, feeding, and predator escape. Ideal for establishing dense wildlife habitat, loafing areas, and nesting cover, Upland Game Mix creates durable food and cover in a single, easy-to-manage seed solution.

458472.name: Dryland Pasture Mix
458472.short_description: Dryland Pasture Mix is engineered for semi-arid landscapes where water is scarce but pasture productivity still matters. This drought-tolerant seed blend establishes a resilient grazing stand for horses, cattle, sheep, and goats, helping you maximize forage yield on low-moisture pastures. Designed to revive overgrazed or depleted dryland fields, it creates dense forage cover that protects soil, reduces erosion, and enhances seasonal feed availability. The mix blends forage grasses and forage legumes chosen for rapid establishment, persistent growth, and compatibility with grazing systems. Whether you’re renovating neglected pastures or establishing new semi-arid pastures, Dryland Pasture Mix supports healthy, multi-species grazing with improved soil moisture retention and forage density—so you can sustain livestock with less irrigation and more resilience over time.
458472.description:
Dryland Pasture Mix is engineered for semi-arid landscapes where water is scarce but pasture productivity still matters. This drought-tolerant seed blend establishes a resilient grazing stand for horses, cattle, sheep, and other livestock across the intermountain West, High Plains, and other regions with less than 15 inches of annual precipitation.

The blend prioritizes proven dryland species: native and introduced grasses with deep root systems that tap subsoil moisture, legumes for nitrogen and palatability, and forbs that add mineral diversity to the forage base. Every species is selected for establishment success without irrigation, long-term persistence under grazing pressure, and nutritional value for a range of livestock.

Seed in early spring or late fall (dormant seeding) into a firm, weed-suppressed seedbed. Our 50 lb bag covers up to 50 acres at a light overseeding rate, or is suitable for 5–10 acres of new establishment. Developed in partnership with our in-house pasture specialists for the specific conditions of dryland ranching across the Western U.S.

458471.name: Premium Irrigated Pasture Mix
458471.short_description: Premium Irrigated Pasture Mix is a purpose-built forage blend designed for intensely managed, irrigated grazing programs. It delivers rapid establishment, dense ground cover, and high-yield production under pivot or wheel-line irrigation, supporting beef and dairy operations that practice strict rotational grazing. The mix also provides high-quality, low-dust forage for horses, making it suitable for strip grazing and sacrifice paddock recovery. Farmers and ranchers can expect improved pasture utilization, longer grazing windows, and better stand resilience across seasons. This premium seed blend tolerates irrigation variability while maintaining forage quality, rumen-friendly fiber, and steady regrowth after grazing. Ideal for multi-species pastures and high-intensity grazing plans across dairy, beef, and equestrian settings.

458470.name: Native Cabin Grass Seed Mix
458470.short_description: Native Cabin Grass Seed Mix is a low-mow, drought-tolerant blend of five native grasses — Little Bluestem, Sideoats Grama, Virginia Wildrye, Canada Wildrye, and Purpletop Tridens — designed to create a soft, naturalistic lawn around cabins, rural retreats, and low-input properties. Mow once or twice a year. No irrigation needed after establishment.
458470.description:
Most cabin properties get mowed twice a season if they're lucky. Native Cabin Grass Seed Mix was built for exactly that — a yard that looks right without requiring you to be there every weekend.

The blend combines five native grass species that do different jobs. Little Bluestem anchors the mix with dense, drought-tolerant clumps and reliable fall color. Sideoats Grama adds warm-season structure and distinctive oat-shaped seedheads. Virginia Wildrye and Canada Wildrye establish quickly, filling ground in the first season while the slower species root in. Purpletop Tridens rounds it out with showy summer seedheads and vertical interest. Together, they create a yard that matures from a naturalized lawn into a low-maintenance native stand over 12–18 months.

The result holds at 6–10 inches with one or two seasonal mows — late fall or early spring is all it needs. Adapted to full sun through light shade, well-drained loam or sandy soils, and pH 5.5–8.0. Seeding rate is 10 lbs per 10,000 sq ft for new seedings or overseeding thin areas.

Unlike turf grasses that need consistent irrigation and fertilizer to look presentable, this mix becomes more drought-tolerant each year as root systems deepen. It thrives on neglect, which is the point. Whether you want to naturalize a cabin clearing, reduce mowing on a rural lot, stabilize a slope along a driveway, or create a buffer between mowed areas and woods, this mix transitions the space without fighting the landscape.

Suitable for USDA Zones 3a–8a. Plant in early spring or late fall for best germination.

458469.name: Mustard Biofumigant Blend Cover Crop Seed Mix
458469.short_description: Choose the Mustard Biofumigant Blend Cover Crop Seed Mix for a fast, short-season solution to pest and disease pressure in vegetable beds. This mustard-dominant mix acts as a natural biofumigant, releasing bioactive compounds that help suppress soil-borne fungi, nematodes, and some bacterial pathogens as the mulch is incorporated. Ideal for breaking pest and disease cycles between harvests, it quickly forms dense biomass that boosts soil organic matter and soil structure. When mowed and integrated as a green manure, the blend enriches the root zone, enhances microbial activity, and improves nutrient cycling, paving the way for healthier transplants and higher yields in subsequent crops. Suitable for cool- and warm-season rotations, easy to sow, and compatible with organic systems.

458468.name: Jimmy's Perennial Wildflower Mix
458468.short_description: Jimmy’s Perennial Wildflower Mix offers a reliable, long-lasting solution for cottage-style borders that calmly return and expand each year. This versatile seed blend naturally naturalizes meadows, fence lines, and acreage edges with a low-maintenance perennial bloom display that requires minimal upkeep. Plant once for a carefree, year-round tapestry of color, texture, and pollinator-friendly nectar. The mix features a balanced selection of hardy perennials that establish quickly, spread modestly over time, and resist common garden stresses. Ideal for borders that echo traditional country gardens, pollinator habitats, and low-water landscapes. With repeated flushes of seasonal bloom, your landscape gains sustained charm without frequent replanting, erosion control, or heavy maintenance. Create welcoming, evergreen-like color that grows richer year after year.
458468.description:
Seed Mix Composition

Species % of Mix
Shasta Daisy 16%
Coreopsis, Lance-Leaved 16%
Pygmy Lupine 16%
California Poppy 10%
Western Blue-Eyed Grass 10%
Mexican Primrose 8%

Yarrow, Western 6%
Black-Eyed Susan 6%

Why This Mix Works

Every species in Jimmy's Perennial Wildflower Mix is a true perennial — plant once and enjoy blooms that return and spread year after year. The blend is designed for maximum color diversity across spring, summer, and fall, with overlapping bloom windows so your landscape is never without flowers.

What You'll See

  • Spring: California Poppy and Pygmy Lupine lead the show with bold oranges and purples
  • Summer: Shasta Daisy, Black-Eyed Susan, and Coreopsis take over with whites and golds
  • Fall: Western Yarrow and Mexican Primrose carry color into late season

Growing Conditions

  • Sun: Full sun to partial shade
  • Water: Low to moderate — drought-tolerant once established
  • Soil: Adaptable to most well-drained soils
  • Zones: Performs across USDA zones 4–10

Planting Tips

Scatter seed on prepared soil in early spring or fall. Press gently into the soil surface — do not bury deeper than ¼ inch. Keep moist for the first 2–3 weeks until germination. Once established, these perennials require minimal watering and no fertilizer.

All seed is independently tested, filler-free, and non-GMO. Questions? Our seed experts are here to help — call 801-531-1456 or email customercare@naturesseed.com.

458467.name: Pasture Clover Mix for Waterfowl Food Plots
categories: Drought-Tolerant Lawn Seeds — Built for CA, AZ, OR & the Southwest
458467.short_description: Establish a high-protein pasture clover mix designed for moist or seasonally flooded fields to attract ducks, teal, and other waterfowl during migration and wintering. This seed blend provides dependable forage and seed heads for bobwhite quail and other upland game birds along pond margins, slough edges, and low pastures. The mix thrives in wet soils and gradually yields dense cover, creating a reliable food plot that sustains birds through thin forage periods. Use it to improve habitat along wetlands, farm margins, and grazing lands while delivering protein-rich forage, early-season greens, and attractive seed heads. A versatile choice for wildlife managers seeking consistent attraction and improved upland bird habitat across wet and transitional landscapes.

458434.name: Clover Lawn Alternative Mix
categories: Drought-Tolerant Lawn Seeds — Built for CA, AZ, OR & the Southwest
458434.short_description: A low-mow clover and microclover lawn alternative that replaces traditional grass with a soft, walkable green carpet. Stays lush with less water, no fertilizer, and far less mowing — ideal for eco-conscious homeowners.
458434.description:
The Lawn Alternative Clover Mix gives you a beautiful, low-maintenance ground cover that replaces or complements traditional turf. Blending White Dutch Clover, microclover, and complementary species, this mix forms a dense, soft-textured lawn that stays green through summer without the chemical inputs or frequent mowing that grass demands.

Clover is a natural nitrogen-fixer — it feeds itself from the air, meaning you can skip synthetic fertilizers entirely. It handles foot traffic well, tolerates drought better than cool-season grasses, and produces gentle blooms that pollinators love. This makes it a perfect choice for families, dog owners, and anyone who wants a functional, low-cost lawn that's also good for the environment.

Our blend is expertly proportioned for quick establishment and season-long coverage. Seed in spring or fall into a prepared seedbed. Works as a standalone lawn or blended into existing turf for a natural, sustainable upgrade.

458047.name: Hardy Grass Seed Mix for High Traffic Lawns
categories: Drought-Tolerant Lawn Seeds — Built for CA, AZ, OR & the Southwest
458047.description: Find a premium grass seed mix that is ideal for high traffic lawns and will stand up to abuse from dogs, kids, and more. Our hardy mix features top-rated varieties that are drought tolerant and create dense, durable turf.

456233.name: Sundancer Buffalograss Lawn Seed
categories: Drought-Tolerant Lawn Seeds — Built for CA, AZ, OR & the Southwest
456233.short_description:
The most popular xeriscape lawn replacement in the US. Uses 75% less water than cool-season turf and stays soft, walkable, and green on rainfall once established.

Sundancer Buffalograss is a native, warm-season lawn grass that stays green and beautiful with up to 75% less water than conventional turf. Perfect for drought-prone regions, it requires minimal mowing and no synthetic inputs once established.
456233.description:
Sundancer Buffalograss (Bouteloua dactyloides) is one of the most water-efficient lawn grasses available — a native North American species naturally adapted to heat, drought, and hard clay soils. Sundancer is a selected cultivar bred specifically for improved density, color, and wear tolerance compared to wild-type buffalograss, making it a genuine premium lawn option for water-conscious homeowners across the Great Plains and Southwest.

Once established, Sundancer needs irrigation only during extended drought — dramatically reducing your water bill and maintenance time. It grows to a tidy 4–6 inch height without mowing, turns a rich blue-green through summer, and goes naturally dormant (tan) in winter before greening back up in spring. No fertilizers, no pesticides, and no constant watering required.

This is a warm-season grass best suited to USDA Zones 3–9 in the central and western U.S. Seed in late spring when soil temps exceed 60°F. Our 3 lb kit covers up to 600 sq ft of new lawn or larger areas as a mix with other native species.

455414.name: Green Screen Food Plot Mix
455414.short_description: A high-attraction food plot seed blend designed to hold deer and wildlife on your property through fall and winter. Fast-establishing annuals and perennials provide reliable forage from early season through hard frosts.
455414.description:
Green Screen Food Plot Mix is engineered to attract and hold deer, turkey, and other wildlife from early fall through late season. The blend combines fast-germinating annuals with persistent perennials to give you green, palatable forage exactly when hunting pressure peaks and natural food sources decline.

The mix includes species proven to draw heavy browse pressure: brassicas for cool-season attraction, clovers for warm-season protein, and grains that remain standing through early frosts. Together they create a food plot that produces from the first cool nights of fall through the end of deer season — giving wildlife a reason to stay on your land.

Seed into a well-prepared seedbed in late summer for fall establishment. The 10 lb kit covers approximately one acre in average soil conditions. Developed by Nature's Seed wildlife specialists with regional foraging behavior in mind.

455409.name: Krunch N Munch Food Plot Mix

452626.name: Pet & Kid Friendly Low-Maintenance Fescue Lawn Bundle

452364.name: White Clover Seed
452364.description: White clover (Trifolium repens) is one of the most valuable and versatile plants you can add to your pasture, lawn, or food plot. This low-growing perennial legume is prized worldwide for its ability to naturally enrich soil through nitrogen fixation, reducing the need for synthetic fertilizer and boosting the growth of surrounding grasses. White clover forms a dense, spreading mat of foliage that can reach up to 12 inches in height, making it an ideal ground cover for erosion control, weed suppression, and improving soil health over time.

451810.name: White Dutch Clover Soil & Grass Health Boost - 5lb for 10,000 Sq ft.

M-Binder tackifier is a botanical glue used in hydroseeding, to stabilize soils and for dust control. Derived from the seed of the plantego plant (Plantago insularis), M-Binder is 100% organic, non-toxic and biodegradable. Use anywhere you need to “tack” down seed, straw or mulch, or to control dust and erosion. Works great for revegetation and restoration projects, fire rehabilitation, landscaping and beautification.

Application

M-Binder may be applied as a dry powder or as wet slurry to dry or wet surfaces. It may even be applied during rain. It does not require set-up or drying time because when it is wet it is a heavy muciloid material and when dry it is a firm but rewettable membrane.

Application Rates

General Use: 60-140 lbs. per acre (approx. 1.5 - 3.25 lbs./1000 sq. ft.)

Mixed with Wood Fiber or Paper Mulch: 80-100 lbs. per acre

Dust Control Applications: 150-200 lbs. per acre

447115.name: Sun and Shade Grass Seed Mix
categories: Drought-Tolerant Lawn Seeds — Built for CA, AZ, OR & the Southwest
447115.short_description: Conquer the shady, humid climate of the American Northeast with this special mix of Kentucky bluegrass and fescue seed. Together these grasses provide quick establishment and a beautiful, dark green lawn anywhere in this area of the country.
447115.description:
Sun and Shade Grass Seed Mix is a balanced blend of Kentucky Bluegrass, creeping red fescue, and perennial ryegrass designed to perform across the full range of light conditions — from full-sun open lawns to partially shaded areas under trees and along building foundations. Most lawns have both, and this blend adapts to them all.

Kentucky Bluegrass provides the fine-textured, dense turf that self-repairs through underground rhizomes. Fine fescues thrive in shade and low-fertility soils where bluegrass struggles. Perennial ryegrass germinates in as few as 5–7 days, providing quick cover while the slower species establish. Together, they create a resilient, self-balancing lawn that fills in naturally based on where each species performs best in your yard.

This blend is expertly proportioned for the Northeast, Mid-Atlantic, and Upper Midwest — regions with humid summers and cold winters where a diverse mix outperforms single-species plantings. Seed in early fall for optimal establishment. Our mix is filler-free, independently tested, and backed by Nature's Seed's germination guarantee.

445350.name: California Poppy
445350.short_description: California Poppy (Eschscholzia californica) is the iconic golden wildflower of the Western U.S., beloved for its brilliant orange blooms, extreme drought tolerance, and ease of establishment. Perfect for meadows, roadsides, and low-water garden beds.
445350.description:
California Poppy is one of the easiest and most rewarding wildflowers you can grow. Native to California and the Southwest, this annual and short-lived perennial thrives in poor, dry soils where other plants struggle — blooming reliably from spring through fall with minimal care. Its brilliant gold and orange flowers close at night and open with the morning sun, creating a dynamic, living display that pollinators and people both love.

Once established, California Poppy reseeds prolifically, building a self-sustaining colony that returns year after year. It requires no irrigation once established, needs no fertilizer, and handles the heat of California summers without the stress that wilts most flowers. This makes it an ideal choice for xeriscaping, meadow restoration, and wildfire recovery seeding across the Western U.S.

Sow seed directly in fall or early spring into a prepared, weed-free seedbed. Scatter seed and lightly press into soil — do not cover, as California Poppy needs light to germinate. Our pure seed is independently tested for germination and free of filler species or grasses.

445349.name: Coastal California Wildflower Seed Mix
445349.short_description: A stunning blend of California coastal native wildflowers selected for drought tolerance, salt spray resistance, and year-round bloom interest. Brings vibrant color to coastal gardens, roadsides, and restoration sites while supporting native bees and pollinators.
445349.description:
The Coastal California Wildflower Mix brings together native wildflower species specifically adapted to California's coastal climate: cool summers, mild winters, salt-laden air, and the lean, sandy or clay soils common to coastal bluffs and hillsides. Every species in this blend is tested for performance in coastal conditions — not just California overall, but the specific challenge of the coastal zone.

The mix includes a rich diversity of annual and perennial natives that bloom in succession from early spring through summer, providing a continuous color display and a reliable nectar source for native bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds. Species are selected to reseed naturally and build in density over time, reducing maintenance needs each season.

Ideal for coastal home gardens, restoration projects, and Cal Fire defensible space zones. Seed in fall (October–December) to take advantage of winter rains for natural germination. Our blend is collected from California ecotypes where possible, expertly tested for coastal adaptability, and packaged filler-free for pure, predictable results.

445347.name: Narrowleaf Milkweed Seed
445347.short_description: Narrowleaf Milkweed (Asclepias fascicularis) is the essential Western U.S. host plant for Monarch butterflies. Plant it to support Monarch migration, provide nectar for native bees, and restore native pollinator habitat in your garden or landscape.
445347.description:
Narrowleaf Milkweed is the native milkweed of choice for most of the Western United States. Unlike Tropical Milkweed (Asclepias curassavica), which can disrupt Monarch migration patterns, Narrowleaf Milkweed is a true native perennial that goes dormant in winter — naturally cuing Monarchs to continue their migration south. Planting native milkweed is one of the most impactful things you can do for Monarch butterfly conservation.

Beyond Monarchs, Narrowleaf Milkweed's small pink and white flower clusters are rich in nectar and attract a wide range of native bees, beetles, and other beneficial insects. It spreads slowly by underground rhizomes to form a naturalized colony over time, providing reliable, low-maintenance pollinator habitat that improves each year.

Native to California, Oregon, Washington, Nevada, and neighboring western states. Thrives in well-drained soils, full sun, and is highly drought tolerant once established. Direct sow in fall for natural cold stratification, or cold-stratify seed for 30 days before spring planting. Our pure seed is sourced from Western U.S. ecotypes for the best regional adaptation.

445346.name: Microclover Seed (Micro Clover, Mini Clover)
445346.short_description:
The best-looking lawn alternative for xeriscape: soft, green, walkable, and self-fertilizing. Microclover uses 50–70% less water than traditional turf.

Many years of natural selection have resulted in revolutionary micro-clovers with all the benefits of traditional clover packed into very tiny leaves. Microclover® “spoon feeds” nitrogen to the grass, producing a healthy, dense and naturally green lawn. Helps out-compete weeds, and keeps grass green all season long.

  • All the benefits of traditional white clover packed into very tiny leaves.
  • Tolerates closer mowing than standard white clover.
  • Acts as a natural source of fertilizer.
  • Comes coated and inoculated.

445330.name: Am 120 Standard Mycorrhizal Inoculant
445330.description:
AM 120 Standard is a premium arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) inoculant containing 100% Rhizophagus intraradices(formerly Glomus intraradices), delivering 300 propagules per gram. It’s designed to form a symbiotic relationship with plant roots—extending hyphae networks throughout the soil to enhance water, phosphorus, and micronutrient uptake, improve drought tolerance, and boost germination and biomass production .

Common applications include:

  • Native plant and ecological restoration – excellent for reforestation, slope stabilization.

  • Nursery/greenhouse seedling production – pre-colonize seedlings in trays or pots (e.g., 5 lb per yd³ medium).

  • Agriculture & row crops – side-dress seed furrows or transplant holes at 5–8 lb/acre (or per 30–40″ row); broadcast for cereals, legumes, and vegetables .

  • Turf, lawns, and hydroseeding – spread 1–2 lb per 1,000 ft² or 60 lb/acre; effective with native meadow or turf seeding .

Best Paired With

To maximize the benefits of AM 120:

  1. Direct root contact
    Apply at planting, mixing with seed, or placing around root balls to ensure spores touch roots—dry broadcasting alone limits effectiveness .

  2. Low-to-moderate phosphorus soils
    High phosphorus levels hinder colonization—avoid over-fertilizing before or during application.

  3. Healthy organic soil or growing media
    Use with good-quality potting mixes or tilled topsoil to support fungal establishment; avoid overly sterilized environments .

  4. Complementary sustainable practices
    Pair with minimal tillage, crop rotation, cover crops, and organic amendments to strengthen native soil microbial communities .

How It Works

  • Forms an extensive network of hyphae expanding the root’s reach far beyond its physical extent.

  • Enhances uptake of immobile nutrients like phosphorus, zinc, and copper; improves water access and drought resistance .

  • Stimulates soil structure and carbon sequestration, producing glomalin “soil glue” that enhances water retention and carbon storage .

  • Promotes plant growth, survival, and yield, especially in seedlings and stressed soils; USGS trials confirmed improved germination or biomass in over 70% of tested species .

Guide to Using AM 120

Application Situation Rate & Application Method
Broadcast / Lawn & Seed Spread 1–2 lb per 1,000 ft² (≈60 lb/acre); lightly incorporate or cover with mulch, then water .
Row crops / transplants Side‑dress 5–8 lb/acre in seed furrow or transplant hole; cover with soil at 2–6″ depth .
Nursery media Mix evenly at 5 lb per cubic yard (≈300 k propagules/yd³) .
Hydroseeding / restoration Blend inoculum with seed and organic fertilizer in first slurry pass; mulch afterwards .
Established plants Use root drench or soil injection (e.g., turkey baster) around drip zone—ensure contact, don’t rely on foliar use .

Best Practices

  • Timing: Apply at planting or transplanting for optimal colonization; inoculating established plants requires soil injection near roots.

  • One-time application: Once colonized, additional inoculation isn’t necessary unless soil is disturbed or sterilized.

  • Minimize phosphorus fertilizer: High phosphorus can suppress fungal establishment.

  • Keep spores viable: Avoid sunlight and store in a cool, dry place; handle with a dust mask when dry .

Why Choose AM 120 Standard?

  • Proven single‑species effectiveness across climates from Canada to Costa Rica .

  • High propagule density ensures robust colonization and quicker root‑fungi networks .

  • Versatility for ecological restoration, agriculture, turf, and nursery use.

  • Supports sustainable soil health—enhanced nutrient efficiency, water retention, carbon storage, and soil structure.

Southern US Pasture Seeds & Seed Mixes
Transitional Zone Pasture Seeds & Seed Mixes

445122.name: Organic Seed Starter Fertilizer 4-6-4
445122.description:
Uses

Organic Seed Starter Fertilizer 4‑6‑4 is a versatile, compost-based, slow-release blend designed as a gentle yet effective starter and maintenance fertilizer. Ideal for:

  • Seed starting & transplants – Perfectly balanced (4% N, 6% P, 4% K) to deliver essential nutrients and humus without burning delicate roots.

  • Vegetables, herbs, roots & flowers – Encourages strong root development and healthy growth from early stages .

  • New lawns, sod & overseeding – Ideal for turf establishment, helping seedlings flourish.

  • Landscaping & erosion control – Great for revegetation, native plantings, slope stabilization, and restoration projects.

What It Works Best With

Pair this fertilizer with:

  1. Well‑prepared soil – Loosened, lightly amended substrate ensures optimal granule contact for nutrient uptake.

  2. Organic seed starting mixes – Such as coco coir blends that support moisture control and slow nutrient release.

  3. Appropriate moisture – Light, consistent watering helps trigger nutrient availability and supports root growth.

  4. Organic gardening systems – Approved for certified organic production and safely used around children and pets .

How It Works

  • Slow-release nutrients – Provides nitrogen for foliage, phosphorus for roots, potassium for overall vigor, plus humates to improve nutrient retention and microbial activity.

  • Humus and organic matter – Adds ~5 % humates, enhancing cation exchange and water retention; buffers pH and suppresses pathogens .

  • Supports root establishment – Ideal in-furrow starter for agronomic crops, bedding plants, and lawn seed.

Guide on Using Organic Seed Starter 4‑6‑4

Scenario Timing & Method
Seed trays or blocks Mix into starter medium before sowing (at ~¼ tsp per 4″ pot) for steady nutrient release
Outdoor vegetable beds Broadcast 1 cup per 10 sq ft (≈1 lb N/1,000 sq ft), dig into top 4″ before planting .
Transplants Place ¼ cup in hole or ring around base before transplanting seedlings .
New lawns & sod Spread 25 lb per 1,000 sq ft, thoroughly water, and maintain soil moisture for 2 weeks .
Landscape/new plantings Apply 10–15 lb per 1,000 sq ft before seeding or planting; repeat applications 2–3× per season .

Seedling Feeding Tips

  • Start feeding when seedlings are ~2″ tall with 2 true leaves. Apply at quarter strength or mix into soil to avoid root stress .

  • Avoid overfeeding – slow-release, compost-based nutrients are gentle yet effective; monitor soil moisture and coloration.

  • Post-germination boost – Water in well after application to activate nutrient uptake and maximize root-zone efficacy.

Why Choose 4‑6‑4 Organic Seed Starter?

  • Balanced nutrient profile with elevated phosphorus supports robust root growth.

  • Safe and certified organic, compliant with whole-food growing standards.

  • Boosts soil health long-term, with humates and microbial content enhancing soil structure and fertility.

  • Versatile application across gardening, landscaping, turf care, and ecological restoration projects.

Quick Usage Summary

  1. Mix before sowing – ideal for seed trays or beds.

  2. Band at planting – ¼ cup/transplant hole for veggies and herbs.

  3. Top-dress pre-sod/seed – 25 lb per 1,000 sq ft for lawns.

  4. Water well – consistently after application for best uptake.

444217.description:
TWCA Water-Wise Shade Turf Mix

Our TWCA Water-Wise Shade Turf Mix is a breakthrough solution for lawns struggling under tree canopies, north-facing slopes, and shaded garden zones. Certified by the Turfgrass Water Conservation Alliance (TWCA), this mix delivers exceptional turf quality with 30–50% less water than traditional lawn blends—making it ideal for eco-conscious homeowners seeking lush, shade-tolerant lawns with minimal input.

Premium Shade-Tolerant Composition

  • ‘Lifeguard’ Tall Fescue: Broad-leaved, deep-rooted cultivar with excellent drought tolerance and shade adaptability.
  • ‘Bighorn GT’ Hard Fescue: Fine-bladed, clumping grass that thrives in filtered light and poor soils with minimal care.
  • ‘Enchantment’ Chewings Fescue: Delicate texture and velvet-like feel, great for shady spots and low-mow maintenance.
  • ‘Moonlight SLT’ Kentucky Bluegrass: Dense, carpet-like finish with strong wear recovery and season-long color.

Key Benefits

  • TWCA Certified Water Efficiency: Saves up to half the irrigation needs, cutting both water use and monthly utility bills.
  • Proven Shade Performance: Engineered for light-deprived areas—no more bare or brown spots under trees.
  • Consistent Texture & Color: Delivers a fine-textured, emerald green lawn with uniform coverage all season long.
  • Minimal Maintenance: Grows slowly, needs fewer mowings, and thrives with light fertilization.

Planting & Care Guide

  • When to Plant: Early spring or late summer when highs are between 60–75°F.
  • Soil Prep: Till or aerate compacted soil; clear debris and test for pH between 6.0–7.0.
  • Seeding Rate: 6–8 lb per 1,000 ft² for new lawns; 3–4 lb per 1,000 ft² for overseeding.
  • Watering: Keep topsoil moist with daily misting until grass reaches 2–3 inches tall.
  • Mowing & Fertilizer: Mow to 2–2.5 inches; feed with a low-nitrogen, slow-release fertilizer in early spring and late fall.

Ideal For

  • Home lawns shaded by mature trees
  • North-facing slopes or side yards
  • Under patios, pergolas, and garden structures
  • Public parks and campuses with shaded green spaces
  • Water-conservation landscapes in shaded zones

Why Choose Shade Turf Mix?

Unlike standard turf blends, TWCA Water-Wise Shade Turf Mix is engineered for light-limited areas—delivering premium color, water savings, and soil coverage even where other grasses fail. Whether you're restoring a tired backyard or greening up public grounds, this mix turns shade into an asset.

355918.name: Sunn Hemp Seed
355918.short_description: Sunn hemp grows 6-12 feet tall in 60-90 days, fixes 100-130 lbs of nitrogen per acre, and actively suppresses root-knot nematodes. The dominant summer cover crop for pre-vegetable rotations in warm climates.
355918.description: Sunn hemp (Crotalaria juncea) is a warm-season tropical legume from South Asia that is one of the fastest-growing, highest-biomass cover crops available for summer use in warm climates. Under favorable conditions — zones 8-11 and summer planting in zones 6-7 — sunn hemp can reach 6-12 feet in height within 60-90 days of planting, producing more above-ground biomass per unit of time than nearly any other cover crop species. This rapid growth makes it uniquely effective at shading out summer weeds, building organic matter, and fixing 100-130 lbs of nitrogen per acre in a single short growing window. Sunn hemp's most distinctive agronomic property is its natural suppression of root-knot nematodes (Meloidogyne spp.). Unlike most cover crops, sunn hemp does not merely avoid hosting nematodes — it actively releases allelopathic compounds from its roots that reduce nematode populations in the soil. Research from the University of Florida and USDA shows 50-90% reductions in root-knot nematode egg masses following sunn hemp cover crop cycles, with effects persisting into the following cash crop. This makes it the preferred pre-rotation cover crop before nematode-susceptible vegetables including tomatoes, peppers, squash, and sweet potatoes in southeastern U.S. production systems. Sunn hemp has a hard limitation: it is completely frost-intolerant. It cannot be planted before the last frost date, it will not establish in cool soils, and even a light frost kills the above-ground plant immediately. It does not overwinter anywhere in the continental United States. In zones 6-7, it functions as a summer annual in the window between last and first frost. In zones 8-11, it has a longer planting window and may be planted multiple times in a season. Sunn hemp seed contains pyrrolizidine alkaloids — chiefly trichodesmine and junceine — that can be toxic to livestock, particularly monogastric animals like horses and pigs. (These are different from the monocrotaline found in some other Crotalaria species.) The alkaloids are concentrated in the seed; the foliage of modern low-alkaloid cultivars carries far less, and grazing trials on those cultivars have shown low risk. To keep things simple and safe, use sunn hemp as an incorporated cover crop rather than a forage species, and keep animals away from the seed.

183473.name: Desert Marigold Seed
183473.short_description: One of the longest-blooming native wildflowers in the desert Southwest. Bright chrome-yellow flowers from March through November on near-zero irrigation once established.
183473.description: Desert Marigold is one of the most dependable wildflowers you can plant in an arid landscape. Native to the Sonoran and Chihuahuan deserts of the American Southwest, Baileya multiradiata produces brilliant chrome-yellow, daisy-like flowers from early spring through late fall — often blooming nearly year-round in the low desert zones of Arizona and Nevada. Few wildflowers match its color output per inch of rainfall. This plant is built for drought. Once established, it survives on as little as 6–10 inches of annual rainfall, making it one of the most water-efficient flowering plants available for xeriscape landscaping. It forms attractive, rounded mounds 12–24 inches tall, covered in silver-gray woolly foliage that gives a soft, textured contrast to the golden blooms. It's a workhorse in rebate-eligible water-wise landscapes across the desert Southwest — on the Southern Nevada Water Authority (SNWA) Water Smart Landscapes plant list and AMWUA's recommended plant list for the Arizona desert. For pollinators, Desert Marigold is a steady nectar and pollen source across a long bloom window. Native bees, butterflies, and other beneficial insects work the flowers consistently from spring through fall. It fills a critical ecological gap by providing late-season forage when many other natives have finished blooming. Sowing is straightforward: surface-sow in fall or early spring, press seed lightly into the soil, and keep moist through germination (10–21 days). Fall sowing in Arizona and Nevada takes advantage of natural winter moisture and produces the strongest stands. Germination slows or stalls in hot, dry conditions — avoid summer seeding. Desert Marigold is a short-lived perennial, typically persisting 3–4 years before dying back. It self-seeds readily under the right conditions, so established plantings can maintain themselves in loose, well-drained soils. Plan for occasional overseeding every few years to keep plantings dense.

184723.name: Little Bluestem Grass Seed
categories: Northern US Pasture Seeds & Seed Mixes

184723.short_description: One of the most widely planted natives in NRCS programs and one of the most widespread native grasses in North America. Little Bluestem delivers copper-bronze fall color, exceptional drought tolerance, and easy establishment across zones 3-9.
184723.description: Little Bluestem is one of the most commonly specified native grasses in NRCS conservation programs across the Great Plains — and for good reason. Schizachyrium scoparium is among the most drought-adapted native grasses on the continent, thriving on shallow, rocky, and sandy soils where introduced species fail. Its modest height of 2 to 4 feet makes it more manageable than Big Bluestem while delivering many of the same ecological benefits. For forage producers, Little Bluestem is fair-to-good forage when grazed young — palatability and quality are best on immature growth in early season and decline as the plant matures and stems coarsen. Established stands yield roughly 1.5 to 2.5 tons of dry matter per acre under adequate rainfall. It is not a high-production forage grass by introduced species standards, but it reliably produces on marginal soils that would not support bermudagrass, orchardgrass, or switchgrass at economically meaningful rates. Its strength is consistency on difficult ground. The ornamental value of Little Bluestem is arguably the best of any North American native grass. From October through February, the foliage transitions from blue-green summer color to deep copper, bronze, and rust — punctuated by fluffy white seed heads that catch morning frost and hold well into winter. This performance has driven significant demand from commercial landscapers, native garden designers, and conservation plantings where aesthetics are part of the project scope. For erosion control on slopes, roadsides, and disturbed areas, Little Bluestem is a first-choice species. Its dense root system stabilizes soil quickly, and its drought tolerance means it does not need supplemental irrigation once established — a critical trait for large-scale roadside and reclamation projects. Establishment is more forgiving than Big Bluestem. Most plantings show meaningful stand development by year 2, with full production reached by year 3. Like all warm-season natives, year 1 growth will be modest as the plant invests in root development.
